declarations.docstring: The auxiliary polynomial in matrix-entry variables is irreducible when the matrix size is positive.
The auxiliary polynomial in matrix-entry variables is prime when the matrix size is positive.
If `a` is prime and does not divide `b` in a domain, then the polynomial `C a * X + C b` is irreducible.
Renaming the variables of a multivariable polynomial along an injective map preserves and reflects primality.
